title: The best month is usually the second-best month
subtitle: Why I steer toward the week either side of perfect, and what it buys you.

text: Peak season is peak because of the school calendar.
sub: Not because of the weather. Once you separate those two things, the whole year reads differently — and most of it reads better.

points.label: May
points.value: Green hillsides, cool shade, a sea just warm enough to swim without bravado.

points.label: June
points.value: Long, clear light. The old towns are filling but not yet brimming.

points.label: July - August
points.value: Peak heat, peak crowds, and the meltemi at its strongest in the afternoons.

points.label: September
points.value: Warmest sea of the year, the wind easing, the European holidays over.

points.label: October
points.value: Lower golden light, tavernas beginning to close, first weather systems in.

title: Three questions that choose the week for you

items.head: Swimming, or walking?
items.body: The warmest water is September. The kindest walking weather is May. Those are not the same voyage.

items.head: Can you travel outside term time?
items.body: If you can, the last week of May and the first two of October are the weeks I watch on your behalf.

items.head: How much flexibility do you hold?
items.body: Late October asks for some. A shifted tender port or a shuttered taverna is part of that bargain.

title: One week apart, two different voyages

text: The second-best month still belongs to the islanders.
sub: All the warmth of summer, little of its congestion, at a lower fare. That is not a compromise — it is the better trip, and it is usually available.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then tell me which weeks you can actually travel, and I'll tell you what the Aegean is doing in them.
